item.title: Morgan Stanley capital markets banker in Singapore hired and promoted to MD by rival US bank
item.description:
Hiring can be hard when you're a smaller bank, but there are some benefits you can provide that the big banks don't. Jefferies </news/jefferies-london-pay>, which is has signficiantly grown its Asian banking team in recent years, has just hired an ECM banker </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> and promoted him despite his role remaining the same.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Phillippe Staatz has joined Jefferies as a managing director </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>and head of Southeast Asia equity capital markets. He spent the last seven years at Morgan Stanley, where he had the same title, but at executive director seniority instead. Before that, Staatz was director of investments for Malaysian investment group Plato, and spent over a decade at Credit Suisse.
Jefferies' Asian capital markets team is much smaller than Morgan Stanley's; the latter bank had the #1 ranked ECM book in Asia (excluding Japan) last year, and its book ranks fourth for 2026 so far. Chris Laskowski, vice chairman of banking for APAC for Jefferies, told IFR last month <https://www.ifre.com/people-and-markets/2492634/jefferies-looks-to-north-asia> that the bank has 200 bankers in the region, up from 26 five years ago. For Southeast Asia specifically, IFR said the bank had the 9th ranked ECM book last year but has slipped to 17th position this year so far.
Competition in Asian ECM is heating up, but the focus seems to be on Hong Kong after a record breaking year for IPOs in the country last year. Reuters <https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nomura-weighs-rebuilding-its-hong-kong-equity-capital-markets-business-sources-2026-11-11/> reported this month that Nomura is considering a rebuild of its Hong Kong ECM business after cutting heads in 2023. Jefferies has made several Hong Kong hires, including Chris Lhert, a Goldman Sachs MD and co-head of APAC structured equity.

item.title: Morning Coffee: Goldman Sachs MD demonstrates the art of making Jensen Huang love you. Banker accused of being harsh and abrasive
item.description:
Who is John Underwood at Goldman Sachs? Aside from being the sort of devoted Goldman lifer who joins as an associate, impressively makes MD eight years later and then stays for the next 20 years, we cannot say. But Jensen Huang has reason to seek him out.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
In the depths of Huang's despair, when it seemed women might appear from the woodwork and tales were being told <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/20/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-culture.html>of Huang threatening to pee upon brains, Underwood was there for him in a big way.
Together with Uber founder Travis Kalanick and venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Brad Gerstner, Underwood was reportedly <https://www.ft.com/content/82d3be02-8ac7-4acb-aefa-6e3722ee05cc?syn-25a6b1a6=1>part of a small coterie of persons going around telling everyone what a great guy Huang was and lobbying for his return. Huang was seemingly aware of this, and that now that he has indeed returned, will surely remember Underwood fondly in his financings and investments.
This will be a good thing given NVIDIA's role as the "Central Bank of AI," <https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/nvidia-is-the-central-bank-to-ais-circular-economy-see-where-the-money-goes-da480b61>investing in companies that will have a need for its chips. In August, before his travails began, the Wall Street Journal <https://www.wsj.com/finance/wall-street-pledged-to-mobilize-500-billion-for-nvidiabut-hasnt-put-up-a-dime-1e41f276> reported that an irate Huang invited Goldman Sachs and others to California to arrange a chip financing deal. Huang was irked because $35bn of financing promised in June hadn't materialised. His August summoning resulted in the promise of $500bn of financing from Goldman, Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield and KKR.
Underwood doesn't appear to have been in that particular room. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon </news/david-solomon-goldman-sachs>sat around Huang's August table with Jonathan Gray from Blackstone and others. Neither Solomon nor Gray stuck their heads above the parapet with public support for Huang, but maybe they sent private emojis instead.
Underwood has form in a crisis. In the Silicon Valley Bank crisis of 2023 he reportedly went around <https://fortune.com/2023/03/23/unsung-heroes-silicon-valley-bank-crisis/>persuading policy makers how bad things were. For the moment, all is happy again in the world of NVIDIA and circular chip financing, but if clouds gather Underwood is Huang's man.
Separately, Roberto Hoornweg at Standard Chartered has reportedly been accused of some Huangish elements in his approach to managing people.
Hoornweg is the chief executive of Standard Chartered's corporate and investment bank. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-24/stanchart-probed-top-banker-after-complaints-about-his-conduct> reports that Hoornweg has been the subject of complaints about his harsh management style and abrasive manner. Anonymous letters about culture, fear of retaliation and the demotion and sidelining of women were reportedly sent to the FCA, the Bank of England and the Standard Chartered chair.
No evidence for the complaints was identified. A spokesperson for the bank told Bloomberg: “The anonymous allegations were thoroughly investigated and were not upheld,” following a probe earlier this year. “No evidence was identified to support the claims, and no further information has been provided. We treat any allegation of misconduct seriously and investigate such claims in a robust and timely manner. Roberto retains the full support of the Bank’s leadership as CEO of Corporate & Investment Banking.”
Meanwhile...
NVIDIA wants a new chief compliance officer if anyone's interested. (NVIDIA) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000090/nov23pressrelease.htm>
Joon Kim, the Wachtell Lipton partner and former federal prosecutor is still investigating Huang at NVIDIA's behest. What happens if he finds something? (Bloomberg) < https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/newsletters/2026-11-23/jensen-s-candor-is-satisfactory-now>
Trump thought Huang might go to China. "I said that Jensen, just promise me one thing, you’re going to work hard. I spoke to him last night because I knew what was going on, and I said you got to promise me one thing, you got the, you got the brain. You got everything going. You’re gonna work hard, and if you work hard, there’s nobody can beat you. And he said, I’m gonna work hard." (CNBC) <https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/cnbc-transcript-president-donald-trump-speaks-with-cnbcs-eamon-javers-and-squawk-on-the-street-today.html>
Huang will face questions over NVIDIA's ties to China when he appears Dec. 1 before a closed doors joint meeting of the House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and China Select committees. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-22/spy-chief-says-us-probing-alleged-spy-tied-to-former-nvidia-ceo?cmpid=eveemea&utm_campaign=eveemea&utm_medium=email&utm_source=newsletter&utm_term=261123&utm_content=11737>
Enron's board brought Ken Lay back as CEO in August 2001 to calm the market, and the company filed for bankruptcy 110 days later." (George Noble) <https://x.com/gnoble79/status/2124960416539480266?s=20>
“This is my first day of work,” joked Huang as employees laughed. “I don’t have a computer, so the IT department is going to give me a new PC.” (New York Times) <https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/23/technology/nvidia-jensen-huang-reinstated>
Happy times for investors that added NVIDIA stock during the dip. “Where can you ever find a stock that’s been growing earnings by 98% a year, trading at eight or nine times forward earnings? That’s a multiple that a non-growth company gets punished with. That’s ridiculous.” (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/i-fell-off-my-chair-investors-marvel-as-huangs-return-sends-stocks-rocketing-98131bc6?mod=hp_onevizplusonevertical_pos_1>
Anthropic needs an investment grade rating by 2030 when half its spending commitments begin. If not, it could struggle to pay its bills. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/anthropic-committed-to-spend-900-billion-wall-street-expects-its-debt-to-be-junk-5514d55d?mod=WSJ_home_feature_3_pos_1>
Investment banks have added 200 dealmakers (to 21,800 ) and 200 equity traders over the past 12 months, with front office headcount in the units reaching 13,700. A decline of 100 people in fixed income trading to 16,200 means total front office employee numbers at the top investment banks were 51,700, up by 300 on 2025. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/deal-boom-sees-investment-banks-increase-headcount-for-the-first-time-years-1da687ca?mod=topic_news>
When a Citi investment banker is invited to join MasterCard. "‘You want to get into payments?’ And I said: ‘Absolutely not. How boring.’" (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/dae45568-65cb-4464-8dcf-0d19770c82eb?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Life in Dubai is not normal. There are “shelter in place” on the walls of Dubai nurseries, restaurants recommended in Michelin’s latest food guide are closed and branded products are less available in supermarkets. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/770e588c-9d85-4999-a25a-c01b8c3078d3?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
CVC Partners withdrew its offer for Irca SpA and UBS and Barclays are stuck with with €1.2 billion of committed financing in a takeover dispute that could end in litigation. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-23/ubs-barclays-stuck-with-1-2-billion-debt-as-irca-deal-unravels>

item.title: Goldman Sachs MD who quit for Stripe has emerged at Gregg Lemkau's fund
item.description:
BDT & MSD Partners is a firm with strong ties to Goldman Sachs, </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs> not least via the fact that its co-CEO, Gregg Lemkau </news/2021/02/gregg-lemkau-goldman-sachs-msd-partners>, was once global co-head of investment banking at Goldman Sachs. BDT & MSD does many things, including merchant banking and private equity </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity>, but has made a new push into technology investing this year by launching a new tech fund. The earliest hires for this initiative are some old colleagues of Lemkau.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Semafor <https://www.semafor.com/article/07/27/2026/bdt-msd-partners-buys-into-tech> reported in July that BDT & MSD had hired Goldman Sachs partner </news/goldman-sachs-partners-2026> Darren Cohen, chief investment officer of Goldman Sachs' growth equity team, to lead this fund. Now, it has hired Paul Pate, a former managing director of that same team; Pate's FINRA registration shows him having joined the firm in New York this month.
Cohen's team was previously known as Principal Strategic Investments; CNBC <https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/03/inside-the-goldman-sachs-tech-fund-that-made-25percent-returns-for-7-years.html> reported in 2019 that it operated similar to a VC firm and had achieved annual returns of at least 25% over a seven-year period at a headcount of fewer than 30.
Pate left Goldman in 2024 to work for payments giant Stripe </news/stripe-s-top-engineers-are-producing-10x-as-much-as-they-did-in-2024> as a strategy lead. He left Stripe in July, around the time Cohen's arrival at BDT & MSD was announced, but he initially left to join growth equity firm Springcoast Partners as a partner. Pate did not respond to a request for comment as to why he departed the firm so quickly.
Growth investing isn't an entirely new concept to BDT & MSD Partners. Semafor reported that it had already raised $832m for a small initial growth fund last year which has stakes in OpenAI </news/sam-altman-goldman-sachs-intern-openai> and Revolut.
BDT & MSD Partners did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Hudson River Trading's hardware team hired another D.E. Shaw veteran after OpenAI detour
item.description:
GPUs </news/quant-trading-gpus> are the trendy hardware for quant firms </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> but other, niche latency-focused chips like ASICs (application-specific integrated circuits) are still beloved. Last year, Hudson River Trading </news/pay-for-electronic-trading-graduates-is-soaring-1m-at-hrt-850k-at-jane-street> made several senior hires from hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> D.E. Shaw's research arm to grow its ASIC engineering team; now it has brought in one more D.E. Shaw alum after a stint at OpenAI.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Anthony Forte joined Hudson River Trading this month as a mechanical engineer. He spent almost the last two years as a member of technical staff at OpenAI, but spent ~17 years before that at D.E. Shaw Research. Other D.E. Shaw Research alums at HRT include Timothy Correia, </news/top-quant-engineer-leaves-de-shaw-biotech-job-for-finance-at-hudson-river> Jeffrey Butts, Brannon Batson </news/another-d-e-shaw-hardware-specialist-defects-to-hudson-river-trading> and Roy Mader, each of whom joined the firm last year. The five men spent an average of more than 14 years working at D.E. Shaw before eventually turning up at HRT.
What makes D.E. Shaw's research arm so attractive to HRT? Its most renowned project is Anton, an ASIC-powered supercomputer used for the simulation of molecular dynamics. Forte is one of the people credited for Anton 2, <https://awards.acm.org/award-recipients/forte_7656042> the second generation of the computer, which won a Gordon Bell Prize for supercomputing in 2014.
ASICs are, in a way, the opposite of GPUs. The latter are designed to be highly versatile. ASICs are highly specialized with unparalleled speed but, once designed, cannot be reprogrammed. For this reason, many firms using low-latency hardware instead opt for field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), which can be 'coded' after being deployed using languages like Verilog. HRT uses these too according to internship listings for its hardware team. The firm's head of AI, Iain Dunning, said last year that "all of the latency has been arbitraged for the most part" in finance, but the firm seems to believe there's room to be even quicker.
Forte's experience at OpenAI may also be a boon to HRT's AI compute stack. In June, the lab unveiled Jalapeño, <https://openai.com/index/openai-broadcom-jalapeno-inference-chip/>a custom ASIC chip designed to speed up AI inference and "deliver performance per watt substantially better than current state-of-the-art" chips. It's not clear how involved Forte was with this project, but he is credited on an OpenAI patent focused on using a stiffener ring to improve the longevity of semiconductors.

item.title: Hong Kong hedge fund veteran shows how it's done
item.description:
If you are Larry Chen it has probably been a very good month.
Chen, who runs single family office Anther Capital in Hong Kong, unwound his $3.9bn of AI bets in the third quarter according to Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/hong-kong-family-office-unwinds-3-9-billion-of-bets-around-ai>analysis of Anther's 13F filings.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Since the end of September, the Nasdaq 100 has fallen 17%.
Chen's impeccable timing has not gone unnoticed by equities hedge fund managers in New York, many of whom are stinging from overexposure to the AI trade.
Chen may have had some help in his call. Alongside his standalone family office, he runs hedge fund Tairen Capital. 13F filings for Anther and Tairen show they cut their combined holdings of US-listed chip and hardware stocks by 99% in the third quarter, from $4.8bn to $58m.
Chen co-founded Tairen in 2007 and so has plenty of experience of difficult markets.
He is not to be confused with another Larry Chen who founded an online tutoring company and lost billions <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-24/bill-hwang-s-implosion-bruises-billionaire-teacher-from-china>in 2021. As he lost money, that Larry Chen declared that he kept telling himself he was “part of a beautiful life” and “things are so good.” US hedge fund traders could try this too.

item.title: Goldman promoted a group of top technologists: London and India may have been particularly lucky
item.description:
Unlike some banks, Goldman Sachs </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs> does not promote MDs every year. Instead, it alternates between promoting new MDs and promoting MDs into partners. </news/goldman-sachs-partners-2026> This can mean that fast-rising VPs who narrowly missed promotion one year have to wait at least two years for a second chance. For the bank's top technology staff, there's another promotion that happens every two years to fill that gap.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Last week, Goldman Sachs promoted a new group of tech staff into 'Tech Fellows. </news/goldman-sachs-tech-fellows>' This is a title given to its most technically gifted employees from VP and up, and gives them the opportunity to join interesting company-wide tech projects <https://www.businessinsider.com/inside-rise-wall-street-tech-fellows-distinguished-engineers-2024-12> in the bank.
We have seen 18 tech fellows publicly announce their promotion; eight are based in India, predominantly in Goldman's Bengaluru global capability centre (GCC) </news/h1b-visa-changes-goldman-sachs>. One of the eight is Swapnil Dey, a VP working on agentic AI and developer AI tools. He has spent over a decade with the bank, joining as an analyst in 2016. Another new fellow, Nitish Gupta, works on architecture for SecDB, Goldman's famed pricing and risk management system for markets. Last year's MD promotions </news/goldman-sachs-managing-directors-2025> were also particularly gracious to Goldman's Bengaluru and Hyderabad offices, with a record 43 MDs being minted there.
Five of the 18 new tech fellows work in London. They include Saravanan Chettiar and Geoff Brown, who joined the bank together as interns, then as graduates. Chettiar works on cloud platforms and dev experience while Brown works on site reliability engineering for Goldman's consolidated trade ledger. Another new European tech fellow is Mats Ljungqvist, a Stockholm-based engineer for Goldman's core equities trading platform.
Three of the newly promoted technologists work in Goldman's New York base. They include Amit Shelawala, an engineering lead for transformation projects, and Luke Tigaris, head of mobile development for Goldman's market insights platform, Marquee.
Goldman's full class of fellows is presumably much larger than this. In 2024, it promoted 111 technologists to fellows. There may be some groups underrepresented; for example, all of the 18 fellows we have seen were VPs or executive directors, but MDs often get the chance to become tech fellows too. The bank did not comment on whether that had occurred this year, nor on the size of this year's class.
Goldman also occasionally bestows the title of tech fellow upon new hires. In July, it hired senior Microsoft director Ravi Teja <https://evidentinsights.com/bankingbrief/ai-manifest-destiny>as a tech fellow as well as its global head of agentic AI. That month, it also hired Maciej Machulak as a tech fellow; he was previously a distinguished engineer at UBS.

item.title: A former JPMorgan trader hired a top HSBC trader for his new hedge fund pod in Singapore
item.description:
The streets of London are flowing with the detritus of damaged macro hedge funds </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>but Singapore is still doing fine. Nothing out of the ordinary is occurring there, say headhunters. Amidst the ordinariness, one man is building a new macro pod at Verition.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The man is Charles Chung, a former JPMorgan trader who joined Verition a few week ago after a stint at Balyasny.
Chung is hiring. He's picked up Alua Collevecchio, a top FX options trader from HSBC in Singapore. He's also thought to have hired Michael Wan, a senior economist from MUFG and another portfolio manager of unknown provenance.
Neither Chung nor Wan nor Collevecchio nor Verition responded to a request to comment for this article.
Chung spent four and a half years at Balyasny and left in May according to the Singapore Monetary Authority Register. Collevecchio spent her entire career 15 and a half year at HSBC. Wan, whose move has not been confirmed, spent the last few years as a senior economist at MUFG.
Verition generated returns of exactly 0% </news/hedge-fund-performance-2026> after fees in the year to September according to Bloomberg.

item.title: Compensation for engineers in French banks is distinctly average
item.description:
When we analysed the top paying tech jobs in London </news/highest-paying-tech-jobs-london>, we found that top financial services firms predominantly paid above average. The same is not true across the Channel; while some smaller firms offer excellent pay, the big French banks </news/bnp-socgen-credit-agricole-q1-2026>are lacking.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Levels.fyi <https://www.levels.fyi/heatmap/europe/>has provided a compensation heatmap for Europe, detailing average pay in France </news/2018/10/french-quant-pay> and the top paying employers for engineering talent. We have added analysis of all-time pay data from Levels.fyi for those top employers as well as several financial services firms. Across all firms analysed, SocGen </news/socgen-london-cuts> and BNP Paribas </news/bnp-q3-2026> employees reported the lowest engineering compensation, each averaging ~$68k. The median compensation for a software engineer in France is $68.7k. Credit Agricole was the exception, paying $78k on average, but the sample size was significantly smaller than the other French banks.
Other finance firms seem to be much more generous. Morgan Stanley paid over $111k on average, higher than AdTech firm Criteo, which Levels had ranked as one of France's top three employers. The US bank only had eight datapoints, however, compared to 50+ at the French banks and 150 at Criteo.
One of the quiet giants for Paris tech pay is Qube Research and Technologies (QRT) </news/qube-research-and-technologies-has-been-hiring-heavily-paying-less>, a quantitative hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> spun out of Credit Suisse, which has ballooned in size in recent years. Levels.fyi data suggests that it pays an average compensation of $160k, more than France's darling AI lab, Mistral.
The structure of pay varies significantly. Google, the top-ranked firm for tech pay in Paris, paid the highest proportion of stock as part of its compensation package. QRT paid the most in bonuses by a significant margin.

item.title: Which is the best bank to work for ever? There could be only one
item.description:
Every year, we run our Ideal Employer </ideal-employer> survey. In it, we ask thousands of financial services professionals – this year 19,000 of them – who they want to work for in the industry. And in 2023 </news/2023/11/best-investment-bank-to-work-for>, 2024 </news/ideal-employer-2024-winner>, 2025 </news/best-place-to-work-finance>, and now 2026, they’ve always had the same answer.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/signup>✍️
For the fourth year in a row, JPMorgan was voted the Ideal Banking Employer </ideal-employer> by our database. Its victory was less dramatic than in previous years – it received fewer votes than second and third combined. Four years ago, when we first rebooted our survey, it received as many as the rest of the top ten put together.
JPMorgan was an exceptionally well-regarded bank on nearly every metric respondents voted on. It scored unusually high two metrics: voters who chose JPMorgan above others were particularly impressed with the quality of its compensation, and their perceived pride in working for the bank.
In 2025, approximately 28% of voters who selected JPMorgan as their ideal employer had experience working at the firm. In 2026, that figure was just 22%. It’s a significant difference and suggests that the firm’s public reputation, at least, has improved.
What did voters say? “They have the right culture and mindset to do our work,” said a UK-based debt capital markets </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> (DCM) VP working for a rival. “Their absolute dominance in DCM and other corporate finance areas is the proof of that.” Another respondent noted that long-standing CEO Jamie Dimon makes the firm “special”.
Bank of America came second in our ranking. It resonated with voters for offering work with meaning, as well as its flexible work offering. As last year, a significant portion of respondents who chose BofA were present employees. One UK technologist </news/how-to-get-a-technology-job-bank> who works at the firm – and chose it as his ideal employer – said that his bosses “genuinely care about their employees, including their wellbeing and their career development.”
British-based HSBC came third. HSBC’s voters – which were disproportionally working for the firm already, much like BofA – generally respected the firm for its flexible work offerings. They also thought the firm was a place “for someone like [them]”. An APAC-based director, who had previously worked at the firm (but no longer did), selected HSBC as her ideal employer saying that the firm was a “great place to work,” offered “lots of learning,” was “flexible,” and “above all hasn’t lost the human element.”

item.title: Morning Coffee: The ex-Barclays MD who's the "adult in the room" at hedge fund Millennium. Fired for being insufficiently optimistic about tech stocks
item.description:
It takes a certain sort of person to rub along with the multibillionaire founder of a hedge fund. It also takes a certain sort of person to work with that multibillionaire founder as he invests heavily in infrastructure that comes with high short term costs and only long term returns. Ajay Nagpal, a former head of prime services at Barclays, is endowed with the appropriate temperament.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Nagpal is president and chief operating officer (COO) at hedge fund Millennium Management. Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/millennium-ajay-nagpal-profile-2026-11> has a long and glowing profile on him, and declares that Nagpal is charismatic. It quotes one former colleague describing him as "the true adult in the room." Another (or the same) former colleague observed that Nagpal "might have the hardest job in hedge funds." This is because he has to manage both the organisation and Izzy Englander, that colleague observed. Englander isn't "known for his patience," the colleague added.
It's not clear how Englander feels about this characterisation: Millennium declined to comment for the article. Being impatient is not an unusual trait among hedge fund executives and other Millennium employees may be more favourable about their founder's temporal struggles.
Either way, Nagpal clearly knows how to work with Izzy. He's been at Millennium since 2013 and is credited with running the "core" of Millennium, including its non-investing operations, like technology, investor relations, trade settlement and recruiting, and with 'industrializing' them so that Millennium works more like an investment bank. Nagpal's efforts allow Millennium to constantly review the risks of the portfolios in its pods, says Business Insider.
Such high praise is sometimes dolloped upon executives on their way out, but Nagpal appears enduringly central at Millennium. Nagpal seems to have been instrumental in bringing Bobby Jain </news/bobby-jain-jain-global> back into the fold. Nagpal reportedly helped lead Millennium's recent fundraise. Nagpal was "heavily involved" in the sale of a 15% stake in Millennium in 2025.
It's worth knowing about Nagpal if you want to work for Millennium. Not least because Business Insider says he himself can allocate money to portfolio managers, either internally at Millennium or as separately managed accounts.
Nagpal is "just driven and inspiring," one former Millennium leader tells Business Insider. He can, however, allow people to "sink or swim," says another former employee. Maybe this is what an inspiring adult does.
Separately, Marko Kolanovic </news/marko-kolanovic-jpmorgan> isn't the only person to have been fired for being insufficiently ebullient about the future.
The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/047a6fec-f0da-41e1-94f6-f7698e4c8cb0?syn-25a6b1a6=1> reports that pension fund managers have been complaining to the Financial Conduct Authority that they too have been let go for having doubts about booming markets. Some said they had been fired for focusing on the risks of investing in tech, and for missing out on high returns. The FT observes that similar things occurred in the run-up to the bursting of the dot com bubble.
Meanwhile...
Goldman’s trading desk said Friday's selloff spread across systematic investors, as the bank’s Panic Index rose to 9 out of 10. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-20/goldman-says-stock-selloff-has-legs-as-panic-index-nears-maximum>
Goldman Sachs says it's nearer the end than the beginning. “Coming into this week, net exposure on our prime book was at multi-year lows. Globally, positioning is near 10-year lows. We saw HFs sell tech at the fastest pace on record over the last 6-weeks. We have seen aggressive selling from the systematic community." (X) <https://x.com/i/lists/7217219>
Mallika Sachdeva, an MD at Deutsche Bank, observed that Asian chip exporting economies are generating vast trade surpluses - and that these are finding their way back to US capital markets. A slowdown in AI investment could hit chip demand, Asian export earnings and foreign buying of US stocks all at once. (Nixon's Substack) <https://nixons.substack.com/p/the-age-of-fragility?utm_source=substack&publication_id=1933989&post_id=225638648&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=qrn8&triedRedirect=true>
“Seasonally, VIX tends to drop in November, particularly with the Thanksgiving holiday. So it’s almost comical that VIX is up over 85% so far this month. Unfortunately, it is unlikely that the volatility shock is over given ongoing probes into Nvidia’s accounting.” (Bloomberg)
Nvidia last year changed its financial reporting last year to stop splitting out revenue billed through Singapore. Instead if started reporting through customer headquarters. In fact, nearly half of global sales were billed through Singapore. New CEO Colette Kress signed off the change. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/047a6fec-f0da-41e1-94f6-f7698e4c8cb0?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
It's been a good year to be an ABS banker. Sales of bonds backed by data centre leases, auto loans and gym memberships have surpassed $380 billion so far this year, topping issuance of more than $367 billion for all of 2025. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-20/asset-backed-debt-sales-top-post-gfc-record-on-ai-strength>
Once you have fired a client, they are very unlikely to come back. They are much more likely to bear a grudge forever. Deutsche has almost never been in a position where it had such a wealth of profitable business lines that it could afford to treat them lightly. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/bfa66957-73d4-44f1-bea5-6b141c197920>
Commerzbank is working hard to keep its clients ahead of being acquired by Unicredit. "There’s more intensive coverage necessary. There are also a lot of debates, more debates ongoing than you would normally have. " (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-20/commerzbank-working-to-retain-clients-ahead-of-unicredit-deal?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261120&utm_campaign=author_23851719>
UBS CFO Todd Tuckner says the bank is focused on staying in Switzerland. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/ubs-finance-chief-says-he-s-focused-on-staying-in-switzerland?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261122&utm_campaign=author_21003048>
Jamie Dimon wants to set “an example” by finding ways to offset a bank tax increase introduced by the UK government last month so politicians “understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”. This will seemingly mean saving £120m in the UK. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/4dd143d0-0b10-4bb8-ac15-e04702fa8b9a?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Ken Griffin wanted Oxford University, Cambridge, or MIT to back his new top technology school in Florida. They did not proceed. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/business/ken-griffin-citadel-miami-carnegie-mellon-338bcd20?mod=WSJ_home_feature_1_pos_1>
MBA applications at the Dartmouth Tuck School of Business are down 31% on last year. At MIT Sloan they're down 32%. At Wharton they're down 10%. (Forbes) <https://www.forbes.com/sites/annaesakismith/2026/11/19/mba-applications-plunge-at-top-us-business-schools>
“Billionaire families often specify ‘If you want £x by this age, you must have done y’.” Middle-class families tend to avoid being this direct with adult children. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/4cf7587f-a408-42af-9f8f-b3dd814db5c0?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
How it is when you leave your broking job and become a teacher. “After a while of not working my brain began to stagnate. My late mother was a teacher, my wife is a teacher, and my daughter too, and I’d always wanted to teach, but at the time I wanted to make as much money for my family as I could. My job now is more meaningful. I feel like I’m having a really positive impact. You always remember that one teacher; if I’m that one teacher for just one person then I’m happy.” (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/money/family-finances/article/tired-burnt-out-and-bored-with-work-meet-the-middle-aged-neters-83p7dlj7w>
Steve Cohen paid $450m over nine years for 30-year-old Mets pitcher Tarik Skubal. (Espn) <https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/50521081/tarik-skubal-new-york-mets-grade-record-contract>

item.title: The Wilderness Diaries, Episode 7: Ups and Big Downs
item.description:
Writing the first six episodes, I realised I was describing only the negatives, and I felt like a cry baby. So I decided to write something positive for once. It still does not have a happy ending. Quite the opposite.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
One day, shortly before summer, an email arrived from a big institution in the City, following an internal referral. Referrals must be an HR nightmare: the company has to contact you because one of its own employees put your name forward. "You are quite late in the recruitment process," I was told. I got through the screening call, which I still consider useless, and two interviews followed that same week. Both went well, especially the video call with the hiring manager.
Then the HR officer rang. "Congratulations, you are in the final two. I will send you a case study to present to a panel of three, including the hiring manager, who is flying in from the US."
I could not wait. I am usually excellent at presentations, and in a room you can show your personality. After all, I do not understand how anyone can hire for a client-facing role after meeting a candidate only on video calls. It was a Friday, and the presentation was ten days away: two weekends.
Since I was unemployed, those ten days were split between the ongoing job search and the presentation. I put enormous effort into it and spent the final weekend perfecting every slide. I used their corporate font and presentation style. I studied every press release and watched every interview. I wanted to project that I belonged there, that I was already one of them. The stress mounted. I am not prone to headaches, but they came regularly, especially on the Sunday before. I had rehearsed so much that I could only see one outcome. I was sure the other candidate felt the same. Or not.
The 45-minute presentation went very well. The words flowed, the discussion was relaxed, and I answered every question easily, because I knew everything about their company: past, present and future. I left the room telling myself I had no regrets. I had given everything. And I had the job. Surely.
A few days passed. Doubts crept in. Then the phone rang. I was sitting on the couch, and my heart pounded so hard it was unbearable.
Her first words were: "Unfortunately, we are not offering you the role."
The rest was a blur. Something about a close call, a difficult choice between two candidates. I cannot remember a word of it, only the "unfortunately". The call ended. I sank into the cushions and stayed there for an hour. I could not move. Numb.
The experience knocked me out for a week. I was a mental wreck, disgusted with the whole system and with that company. Was it my age? Was it my gender, or something else? I will never know.
I went into hibernation for five days. Usually a sporty person, I could not even go out for a run.
Follow me on X <https://x.com/MadameButcher>. Follow me on LinkedIn. <https://www.linkedin.com/in/sarahbutcherjournalist/>
Hope and disillusion. Such a painful combination.

item.title: Hedge fund Balyasny is closed to new money. What about the $50m+ hiring?
item.description:
Balyasny Asset Management (BAM) is like Goldilocks. After several years spent seeking an optimal amount of assets under management (AUM), it has decided it's just right. Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/balyasny-tells-investors-closed-to-new-capital-2026-11> reported yesterday that the firm has been telling investors it's closed to new money.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The closure comes after a period of heady growth </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-pay-millions>. Once a cosy place where people referred to each other as "Bamily", Balyasny grew assets from around $16bn in May 2022 to around $37bn now. In the process, it roughly doubled investment headcount. In the past two years alone, Balyasny added 212 investment staff according to regulatory filings. </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring>Last year, it was the third most zealous hirer in percentage terms, behind Verition and Jain Global. </news/bobby-jain-jain-global>
Some of Balyasny's portfolio manager hires have come with impressive price tags. In August 2024, Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-08-08/balyasny-goes-on-new-hiring-spree-with-200-million-in-payouts>reported that Balyasny was embarking on a $200m hiring spree. New equities hires like Peter Goodwin and Alberto Mann reportedly joined on packages worth $50m+. David Brodsky </news/dave-brodsky-balyasny-citadel>, a healthcare-focused PM from Citadel, reportedly joined on a similar amount despite an alleged $60m drawdown at Citadel.
Balyasny's recent hiring has been about diversification. Traditionally an equities-focused house, the fund has spread into areas like macro and commodities trading. This year, however, that hasn't worked out so well.
In the year to October, Balyasny lost 2.7% net of fees according to Bloomberg. In October, it lost another 3.4% before fees. It's a far cry from the heady days of 2020 when a less diversified version of Balyasny Asset Management generated returns of 33%. <https://rupakghose.substack.com/p/peak-pod-shop-and-balyasny-blues>
Following October's macro brutality, some of Balyasny's previously prized hires have been leaving. Stanley Sheriff, </news/star-ex-goldman-sachs-trader-retires-aged-33-following-eight-year-hedge-fund-career>a 33-year-old ex-Goldman Sachs macro trader whom Balyasny poached from rival fund Taula, left Balyasny again a few weeks ago. Sheriff was only at Balyasny for approximately 18 months. He spent less than two months at Taula and is thought to have been lured by an eight figure package to join Balyasny. It's thought he left by mutual agreement.
James Watson </news/james-watson-balyasny-millennium>, whom Balyasny hired from Millennium in 2023 also left again last month. Watson, who was a senior macro portfolio manager at Balyasny, is returning to Millennium in a business management role. It's thought that Balyasny also paid eight figures for Watson, who arrived only in September 2024 and was active at the fund for barely two years. Millennium is thought to have wooed him back after what some say was a difficult year for his Balyasny team.
Balyasny is far from the only fund to lose macro portfolio managers this year; hundreds are out of the market. </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up> But with the fund closing to new investors and registering a loss for 2026, eyebrows are being raised at the expensive hiring past. Balyasny was "aggressive" in some of its hiring, say headhunters on both sides of the Atlantic. "In some cases," they paid more than other funds, says one headhunter. Another says junior PMs in particular appeared to have been well paid to join the Bamily.
In other cases, though, Balyasny was outbid. Millennium added the greatest number of investment professionals between 2022 and 2025, </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring> at 395 extra people. Those hires included Steven Schurr, a senior equities portfolio manager at Balyasny, whom Millennium reportedly <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-04-29/millennium-poaches-balyasny-s-schurr-with-100-million-offer> hired for a $100m package in 2025. Balyasny presumably wanted to keep Schurr, who is said to <https://phoenixlearning.substack.com/p/the-best-balyasny-pm-made-250m-in> have made $250m in profits for the firm in 2024, but its pockets don't appear to have been deep enough. Similarly, Millennium poached Max Witcher </news/balyasny-s-big-london-equity-derivatives-guy-appears-to-have-gone-to-millennium>, another profitable equities PM from Balyasny in July.
In their defence, funds wafting eight figure packages typically point out that they are contingent upon performance and include money for team members plus the cost of buying out deferred bonuses from elsewhere. Quietly, though, headhunters say hedge fund pay has become "crazy" and that Balyasny has been just one of the funds participating in the madness.
What next? The decision to close to new cash looks like an admission that Balyasny needs to get a handle on its existing strategies before putting extra money to work in a crowded market. After a difficult year, the fund is still hiring - possibly to replenish its ranks, possibly to fulfil existing commitments. Balyasny recently added Arsenije Dusanic from Trafigura in Switzerland to trade oil. 30 other portfolio managers are thought to be in the pipeline and currently on gardening leave. The eight figure recruiting is not over yet.

item.title: This could be good news for Citi people worried about imminently losing their jobs
item.description:
Citi is cutting jobs. As we have observed, the US bank has made multiple rounds of job cuts </news/citi-s-2026-layoffs-have-been-more-frequent-and-widespread-than-we-thought> this year. Anecdotally, many of its cuts appear to have afflicted staff in areas like regulatory reporting, risk, compliance, KYC and fraud detection. This is occurring both as the bank pursues AI-driven efficiencies and as it approaches the end of transformation work related to the 2020 consent order <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000110465920113933/tm2032793d1_ex99-3.htm> for which it hired thousands of new people.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
As Citi moves into its new target state, though, there are indications that old issues might be surfacing. Reuters <https://www.reuters.com/business/citi-incorrectly-booked-trades-underestimated-risky-assets-by-35-billion-sources-2026-11-19/>reported yesterday that Citi underestimated the risk weighted assets in its European trading unit by $35bn after an error recording some trades. The error reportedly related to the use of an internal Citi risk model rather than a standard model with regulatory approval.
Citi declined to comment for this article, but the bank told Reuters that it "completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers." It added: "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank."
Citi's 2020 consent order was imposed after the OCC regulator found that the bank had "failed to implement and maintain an enterprise- wide risk management and compliance risk management program, internal controls, or a data governance program commensurate with the bank’s size, complexity, and risk profile."
Former Citi CFO Mark Mason </news/mark-mason-citi> said in 2024 </news/citi-lifted-the-veil-on-its-complex-data-issues-and-the-staff-needed-to-fix-them>that the bank was spending $250m on remediation, including new data professionals. In July 2024, Citi was issued a further </news/citi-insiders-complain-of-death-by-powerpoint> $136m regulatory fine for data quality and risk controls relating to commercial loans.
Elements of the 2024 additions to Citi's consent order were lifted last December. Speaking at Citi's May investor day, current CFO Gonzalo Luchetti <https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/investor-day/citi-ID26-financial-overview-presentation.pdf> said that as the transformation work that followed the 2020 order nears an end, costs will be trimmed.
The Federal Reserve didn't comment underestimation of RWA when contacted by Reuters, and the OCC wasn't available. However, the latest issue may encourage Citi to take great care before cutting staff who can help prevent it making future mistakes.

item.title: A Schonfeld guy with a big job title has journeyed to Balyasny
item.description:
Balyasny Asset Management may be closed to new money <https://www.businessinsider.com/balyasny-tells-investors-closed-to-new-capital-2026-11>but it is not closed to new hires. Or at least it wasn't when it hired the new people who are now arriving there.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
One of the new Baly hires is understood to be Amu Latif, a nice man with a large title. Latif was global head of macro trading in Dubai at Schonfeld. Now he is understood to be doing something similar at Balyasny.
Neither Balyasny nor Schonfeld nor Latif himself confirmed the move. But he is there at Balyasny on the Bloomberg terminal and multiple sources assured us of his new seat.
Latif's move comes after Schonfeld coincidentally hired Kevin McDonald from Balyasny as it grows its macro team. McDonald, who has been on gardening leave since March, is joining Schonfeld in New York early next year as co-COO of macro fixed income. Last time he was on garden leave, McDonald was an extra in movies like the Time Travellers Wife. We cannot say if he has done the same this time.
Although Latif's title suggests he's a big deal for Balyasny, multiple source say that head of macro is a head of office type role. Colleagues say Latif is not a big risk taker. But maybe he will help Balyasny hire some new ones.

item.title: Morning Coffee: Bankers face a harder 2027 as tech types in tiny apartments make them feel poor. UBS goes all India
item.description:
If you have spent any time in the presence of Gen-Z you may be familiar with the concept of mogging. This is when someone attractive appears in the vicinity of someone less attractive and makes them appear even more lumpish.
Yesterday, bankers and hedge fund managers were mogged by persons at Anthropic. After the IPO, the average employee at Anthropic is now worth over $40m. <https://fortune.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-millionaire-employees-billionaire-early-hires-wealth-concentration-warning-dario-amodei/> 400 people at Anthropic are worth over $100m. <https://fortune.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-millionaire-employees-billionaire-early-hires-wealth-concentration-warning-dario-amodei/>A 37-year-old technology journalist from Brighton who studied creative writing at the University of East Anglia is among the founders now worth circa $20bn. <https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmd7159vlr85o>Spare a thought for David Solomon at Goldman Sachs with his few hundred million.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Needless to say, bankers have also made money from Anthropic and the AI cloud it floats upon. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2026-11-18/goldman-sachs-and-morgan-stanley-are-high-on-the-ai-trade>notes that the share prices of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley have begun moving in lockstep with the Nasdaq 100 and that 'any kind of tech bust next year will hit bankers and their bonuses hard.'
Is any kind of tech bust coming? Someone who can definitively answer this question will mog a world of pundits. Michael Burry is giving it a good go. <https://michaeljburry.substack.com/>Morgan Stanley's equity strategists are at the mirror <https://www.morganstanley.com/insights/articles/stock-market-investment-outlook-2027>in the other corner. Either way, Bloomberg's Paul Davies suggests <https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2026-11-18/goldman-sachs-and-morgan-stanley-are-high-on-the-ai-trade> 2027 may not be a great vintage in financial services terms. 2026 was a "smash and grab" by the tech sector as it raised money while it was available, says Davies. 2027 will be about digesting the winnings while markets creak under the debt burden and high interest rates mog all risky bets. Already, some data centre loans are being offloaded at 85 cents or so on the dollar. <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-16/hsbc-sold-300-million-troubled-data-center-loan-at-discount>
People in financial services may therefore feel like hoarding their 2026 bonuses. People at Anthropic plan to give them away. The New York Times <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/18/opinion/anthropic-ai-openai.html?unlocked_article_code=1.RVE.AUKz.AkiqfoAGG5ph&smid=url-share> observes that many Anthropic employees 'cram themselves into modest group apartments' and throw alcohol-free parties. Many are effective altruists who want to make the world a better place and believe that donating money in a logically-empowered way will achieve this.
Bankers and hedge fund managers do not describe themselves as effective altruists. Finance is a grind. </news/analyst-to-pm> "People in finance have worked their arse off for years and years to get where they are," says Matthias Schwarz, founder of Career Capital One <https://careercapital.one/about/> and former head of EMEA credit trading at Bank of America. "These are very hard jobs and it takes a long time to get to the top. In markets you get knocked over every day and have to stand back up. You're wary of how quickly this could end and how you might not have a career after the age of 40 or 50." Markets will humble you agrees one senior portfolio manager.
It's a bit different for the new AI multimillion and multibillionaires, says Schwarz. "When you get rich over the course of a few years and it falls into your lap" you're more likely to give much if it away, he suggests.
Separately, a ruinous year seems to be coming for UBS employees in Poland. Having discovered Warsaw and Krakow in 2007 </news/tech-jobs-finance-poland-warsaw> and built offices with around 5,000 people there, Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/ubs-plans-to-shift-hundreds-of-roles-to-india-in-offshoring-push> reports that UBS is now going big on India.
UBS reportedly plans to move hundreds of roles from Poland to India next year. This is in addition to the 3,000 roles it's cutting because of the Credit Suisse integration.
Other banks may yet get the same idea. Bloomberg notes that the Rupee has devalued against major currencies (and the Polish Zloty) in recent years and that this is suddenly making offshore to India seem an even better idea than before.
Meanwhile...
Some Anthropic employees are considering creating private family foundations, which have a 5% annual minimum distribution rule. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/anthropic-ipo-stock-market-today-11-19-2026/card/what-anthropic-wealth-could-do-for-charity-political-giving-ylOGhC9vBPu05x9iUH7b?mod=hp_twovizpluslivelctimeline>
Anthropic's IPO was muddied by its 26bn concurrent private placement to Anthropic’s suppliers of chips, compute and foundry services. These companies invest in Anthropic, which in turn needs to spend enormous sums on the infrastructure they provide. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/4224e2ed-116c-466b-97f4-54a5ef43a54e>
More than half the institutional investors bidding for Anthropic stock got nothing. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/anthropic-ipo-said-to-give-nothing-to-most-institutional-buyers>
Most Anthropic employees (Ants) are not planning to sell their stock. They think it will soon be worth much, much more. (NYT) <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/18/opinion/anthropic-ai-openai.html?unlocked_article_code=1.RVE.AUKz.AkiqfoAGG5ph&smid=url-share>
Brian Moynihan at Bank of America says deals are being postponed into 2027. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-16/bofa-s-moynihan-says-some-deals-are-getting-pushed-into-2027>
Balyasny will not be accepting new money from investors for the foreseeable future. (Business Insider) <https://www.businessinsider.com/balyasny-tells-investors-closed-to-new-capital-2026-11>
The ECB will be taking a long look at banks' prime broking businesses. It's particularly interested in fund financing, asset-based lending, exposures to private equity and credit as well as firms investing in tangible assets. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/ecb-to-probe-riskier-private-credit-hedge-fund-links-at-banks>
An Italian unit at Deutsche Bank hid as much as €800m of losses. Italian managers created a local reserve pot called “tesoretto” — little treasure box — which they used to conceal their failure to meet profit targets. This went on for a decade and they were given large amounts of severance when they were let go. (Financial Times) <https://www.ft.com/content/06be5c7d-b1f2-44e9-9cad-a2dcb5a2f452?syn-25a6b1a6=>
Christian Sewing says clients are calm after the big Deutsche Bank data leak. "This is a totally different bank... Certain issues happened in ⁠the past. They have been worked on." (Reuters) <https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/deutsche-bank-ceo-says-clients-calm-after-data-leak-2026-11-19/>
Deutsche Bank shares are down 9% this week. (FT) < https://www.ft.com/content/e444203b-c639-4cb5-b35a-75829d2d62de?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Deutsche Bank is facing a regulatory investigation into its handling of client data. (Reuters) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-19/deutsche-bank-probed-by-regulator-over-data-handling-after-leak>

item.title: Citadel's new California quant trading business and the non-compete question
item.description:
Jane Street does not usually use non-competes </news/citadel-securities-vs-jane-street>. Citadel does. Citadel's non-competes are often two years </news/citadel-non-compete>, even for its junior staff, but as Citadel moves into Janes Street's territory, it may have to stop hemming people in.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/citadel-bolsters-shorter-term-trading-with-new-california-team>reported yesterday that Citadel is opening a new systematic equities unit in Southern California and that this will engage in short term trades, not unlike Hudson River Trading </news/hudson-river-trading-pay>and Jane Street. It will reportedly be known as Southern California Investments (SCI).
SCI is being run by Alexey Poyarkov, </news/tgs-to-citadel> whom we were first to report had joined Citadel from Irvine California-based quant trading firm TGS </news/tgs-management-company-llc> Management Company LLC in September. Citadel's own website <https://www.citadel.com/what-we-do/global-quantitative-strategies/> confirms that Poyarkov will be running SCI as part of Citadel's global quantitative strategies (GQS) business and that the business will be based in "Irvine California."
Given that Citadel didn't previously have an office in Irvine California, it obviously wanted Poyarkov a lot. Citadel declined to comment for this article, but it seemingly wanted Poyarkov so much that it is also prepared to forego its non-competes.
Non-competes are illegal in California. State laws say that non-competes are void there, even if employees arrive from out of state and have already signed something saying they won't work for two years. Anyone hired by Citadel to Poyarkov's new team in California will therefore be free to leave and to find an immediate job elsewhere.
Given that non-competes are a popular way of protecting proprietary information, it might be supposed that this will dissuade Citadel from hiring California-based employees for Poyarkov's team. However, people familiar with the matter tell us there are other methods of keeping people out of the market in the state and that these involve withholding deferred compensation.
Maybe Citadel plans to do this in Irvine? TGS Management Company may deploy deferrals as a retention tactic, although this hasn't been confirmed with the firm. If Poyarkov hires Irvine-based talent for his new Citadel team, then TGS is the obvious fishing ground. However, Citadel may need to spend heavily to compensate any other TGS recruits if they leave hefty deferrals on the table when they move.
There is a precursor to Citadel's new Irvine office. The firm already has a San Francisco office populated by 18 investment staff according to its most recent ADV form. It's not clear how Citadel operates in the absence of non-competes there.

item.title: Goldman Sachs' most intense MD and the multimillion bonus year
item.description:
James Donovan has known many Goldman Sachs bonus rounds. Having joined the firm out of Harvard Law School in 1993, Donovan is approaching his 33rd Goldman bonus experience. You might think he would be relaxed in the circumstances. But Donovan does not always seem an especially relaxed person.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Aside from being a very long-established Goldman Sachs banker and current vice chair of global client coverage at the firm, Donovan is known as a YouTube micro celebrity. </news/2023/10/jim-donovan-goldman-sachs-120>A 2016 video, 'Are you destined to deal?', <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RpUJfW4WTKw#xd_co_f=ODFkN2I3ZWUtYTI0Yy00ODkzLTgyNTctYzM1ZDRjMjk0YTMw~>featuring him advising students at the University of Virginia has nearly 4m views. A 2023 video, 'The Making of an Investment Banker', <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Pk8EmyK7kw>also featuring him advising Virginia students, has just over 3m.
In neither video does Donovan come across as a cheery folksy person who might be sanguine about disappointment. Based on the videos, he doesn't smile much. “Never ever give up. Adopt that mantra as part of your life. Don’t take no for an answer," he told students in 2023. Seven years earlier, Donovan told the students that he spent the first ten years of his Goldman career, “really, really killing myself, pulling all-nighters.” A large bonus 33 years later might be seen as justification for this grind.
Donovan may indeed be due a large bonus this year. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-16/pentagon-deputy-feinberg-steered-defense-contract-deals-to-his-goldman-banker> reported this week that he's worked on several large deals in 2026, including Lockheed’s $59bn Pentagon deal to triple Patriot missile production, and two RTX contracts worth a combined $45bn+. In this way, one of the 'people familiar with the matter' told Bloomberg that Donovan has set himself up for millions to be added to his bonus.
Sounds great, except there's a catch. Those same people told Bloomberg that US Deputy Defense Secretary and Cerberus co-founder Steve Feinberg suggested that defence companies hire Donovan as their advisor. Donovan has worked with Feinberg for years, and Lockheed and RTX executives reportedly told other Goldman bankers that they felt Pentagon officials had pressured them into working with him.
There is no suggestion that Donovan acted unlawfully, but Goldman reportedly decided to limit the fees it was charging for the deals, while still allowing Donovan to work on them.
It's not clear how Donovan feels about this. He didn't respond to a request to comment on the Bloomberg article. Goldman Sachs declined to comment.
Goldman told Bloomberg: "Like other banks, Goldman Sachs provided financial advice to companies on matters involving the Department of War. We’re proud of our work for our clients.”
The Pentagon told Bloomberg that claims Feinberg directed companies to use Goldman were "categorically false," and that the department had encouraged contractors to hire financial advisers, but that the choice of adviser was entirely theirs.”
Lockheed told Bloomberg it works with a range of advisers and that those relationships are managed in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations. RTX declined to comment.
The implication nonetheless is that Donovan's bonus might be smaller than he'd hoped this year. It also seems that some Goldman bankers might not be feeling generous towards him. Those bankers might be on Goldman's defence team. Bloomberg reports that defence bankers at Goldman flagged concerns about Donovan's involvement on big defence deals and asked at least one client to copy them into emails. Donovan reportedly isn't a specialist in the defence sector and Goldman's defence bankers had been working with the same clients for years.

item.title: Citadel's new partner: A French-educated algorithmic energy trader
item.description:
It has been a tough year for traders in several markets, </news/hedge-fund-performance-2026> especially fixed income and equities. Commodities traders </news/commodities-trading-hiring>have (so far) been spared from these woes and one of the biggest hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> in the space, Citadel, </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel> was up over 15% for the year to October in its flagship Wellington fund. Now, it's bringing in another Commodities specialist as a partner in its London office.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Thomas Lefebvre has joined Citadel as a partner and portfolio manager for global volatility trading according to his Linkedin. Both the FCA register and the UK's Companies House confirm his arrival at the fund, with the latter confirming that he is a member of Citadel's European partnership.
Lefebvre is a veteran commodities trader who was most recently global head of options trading for commodities house Hartree Partners. He built out its proprietary options trading business from scratch with a focus on algorithmic trading according to his LinkedIn. Before that, Lefebvre was a trader at EDF energy, a former Grande École </news/best-grande-ecole-finance> graduate from ENSAM and a recipient of the DEA El Karoui </news/2010/03/students-of-the-french-quant-goddess-are-coming-of-age>. Lefebvre started at ENSAM in 2008, which would likely put him in his mid-to-late-30s.
While other markets have been on a downward trend this year, commodities like oil and power have had their volatility turbocharged by geopolitical conflicts, especially those between Iran and Israel which resulted in the Strait of Hormuz being blocked. It started in February and, even today, <https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/19/iran-war-live-saudi-led-coalition-strikes-yemen-ships-on-fire-in-hormuz> there are reports of oil tankers being set ablaze after hitting mines. Recruiters told us in the summer </news/commodities-trading-hiring-2026?_gl=1*4a9d6z*_up*MQ..*_ga*OTYwNTM1ODc4LjE3OTUwODgwMDc.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3OTUwODgwMDYkbzEkZzEkdDE3OTUwODgwMTAkajU2JGwwJGg3ODA1MDU4NjU.> that commodities trading recruitment was unusually high in Q2 and that the trend was continuing into Q3.

item.title: Hudson River Trading's high-frequency trading lead for Chinese equities is leaving
item.description:
Quant trading firms </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> aren't always known to hire from banks, but it happens. In 2022, Hudson River Trading </news/the-coffee-run-the-kind-trading-firm-paying-1m-to-graduates-and-100m-to-its-top-people> hired Goldman Sachs </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs>' head of electronic market making for Asia - now, he is elsewhere.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Navin Kumar has departed HRT after four years. He was an algorithm development lead working on high-frequency trading strategies in the Chinese equities market. Kumar recently updated his LinkedIn profile to show that he is serving a non-compete until late 2027, but his FINRA registration shows him leaving the firm in May.
Curiously, despite being based in Hong Kong in his previous role at Goldman Sachs, Kumar was relocated to New York for the role. HRT has 5 offices in Asia according to its website, including ones in Singapore, Hong Kong and Shanghai. China has been pushing back against high-frequency trading strategies <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-16/china-clamps-down-on-high-speed-traders-removing-data-servers> in recent years by trying to remove the competitive advantages of firms located close to Chinese exchanges.
Kumar has moved between banks and trading firms across is career. He started his career at now-defunct hedge fund Amaranth, before moving to Goldman to become a quant research </news/quant-jobs-finance>VP. He later worked at Tower Research Capital, the market making firm from which HRT's founders originated, before returning to Goldman Sachs for his market making role. Kumar declined to comment on his future plans.
Someone with his expertise would presumably be welcome at any of the firms expanding their office space in Asia. Jane Street and Susquehanna <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-16/china-clamps-down-on-high-speed-traders-removing-data-servers>are each increasing their office space in Hong Kong while Citadel Securities <https://www.reuters.com/markets/asia/citadel-securities-expands-singapore-sydney-offices-major-asia-push-2026-11-13/> is increasing its office space in Singapore and Sydney.

item.title: Morning Coffee: 26-year-old JPMorgan analyst is now coming for Citi jobs with his AI unicorn. Citadel’s hottest new team is run by its secretive hire
item.description:
Today is, of course, the big day for the paper billionaires and cash multidecimillionaires created by the Anthropic IPO. And it’s also a big day for a lot of tech investment bankers, who will be congratulating themselves on a big deal brought across the line in challenging conditions. But as they prepare the initial investor feedback reports and wash-up presentations and start thinking about what they might be staffed on next, the junior bankers might want to consider what the future holds.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Rogo <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/ex-junior-bankers-ai-startup-rogo-leaps-to-3-75-billion-valuation?taid=1fb97d71-3aa0-41b9-9b2c-6c3c8d29de0c&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>, a startup founded by 26-year old former JP Morgan banker John Willett <https://paw.princeton.edu/article/young-alumni-shake-business-world-ai> and his college friend Gabe Stengel (formerly of Lazard), is the kind of company that Anthropic has made possible, but it’s also potentially going to greatly change the jobs of the bankers who worked on that IPO. It started as a chatbot app for banking, but now it provides a variety of “financial modelling and dealmaking services”. Clients include Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan and Wells Fargo, and then Citi apparently “rolled it out” last week.
The greatest threat to Rogo's valuation ($3.75bn as of the current funding round) seems not to be a lack of appetite on the part of the banking industry for automating processes, but rather the fact that Rogo is now facing competition from Anthropic itself, which also wants to give bankers customised tools to let them generate models, pitchbooks and all the things which used to keep junior bankers up at night.
So far, this has all been spun as good news for junior bankers; graduate hiring hasn’t fallen across the industry, and they are being promised that only the drudgery will be automated, leaving them to take a more active part in the interesting and client-facing parts of the job. The sky is pink and pink only.
And yet, there is only so much client contact to be shared out. And senior bankers tend to be quite cautious about letting people talk at meetings until they’ve proved their worth. And although junior bankers might be encouraged to develop their own ideas at an earlier career stage, this isn’t necessarily as much fun as it sounds; generating a dozen pitches that never get read can be quite dispiriting.
In fact, the most likely way in which junior analysts may be encouraged to take on more senior roles is that instead of receiving “pls fix” emails in the middle of the night, they will be the ones reviewing materials, typing their own “pls fix” messages into chat windows.
While this happens, bankers can look forward to being caught up in a rat race, trying to develop expertise at a quicker rate than it can be commodified. Some people working today, unless they can get a role in developing AI systems like Willett and Stengel, may end up looking back at 2026 as the last good year.
Elsewhere, “Southern California Investments <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/citadel-bolsters-shorter-term-trading-with-new-california-team>” is the new, somewhat uninformatively named systematic equities pod at Citadel. It will be trading in “totally different dimensions of the markets” from the rest of the Global Quantitative Strategies group, according to the head of GQS, Navneet Arora. The dimension in question is time; the new strategy is located in the short-term, high frequency trading space currently dominated by proprietary trading firms like Jump and Jane Street.
Arora seems to have had to do all the press for the new strategy, because Southern California Investments is being run by Alexey Poyarkov </news/tgs-to-citadel>. Poyarkov joined Citadel </news/tgs-to-citadel> from the highly secretive firm that is TGS Management </news/tgs-management-company-llc>back in September, and it seems that he is a lot better at designing trading algorithms than he is at self-publicity. As far back as 2017, he has been “declining to comment <https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-quants-run-wall-street-now-1495389108?st=j5LEBT&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink>” on articles about his mathematical prowess and the enthusiasm of big trading firms to get into bidding wars over him.
Which kind of fits. Short term trading is a game of minuscule advantages, in which every source of edge is jealously guarded, and where it’s quite common to have serious legal battles over intellectual property. A distaste for the limelight is probably a sensible habit to get into when you literally know secrets worth millions of dollars.
Meanwhile …
“It’s bad form to blow up repeatedly … [Leopold Aschenbrenner] really wants to avoid being in that situation again”. And so, as the “Situational Awareness” fund begins to build its public equities portfolio back up again, and to take on leverage once more, they are looking to hire a chief risk officer, and working with a consultant to manage their relations with brokers. From a staff of only eight professionals back in the good old days, SA is now employing thirty people; it’s almost beginning to look like a normal hedge fund. (FT <https://www.ft.com/content/1fcbc6ea-1be3-44d2-b564-8ebf91181639?syn-25a6b1a6=1>)
Citi has settled out of court in the case of Ardith Lindsey, one of the highest-profile sexual harassment cases to have been brought since the law on mandatory arbitration changed in 2022. None of the parties have commented on the settlement which related to some shocking allegations of bad behaviour at the end of a workplace relationship. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/citi-settles-sexual-harassment-claims-by-managing-director?taid=6afd00ce6018910001a162c1&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>)
Deutsche Bank once had a Qatari employee who was so rich that he regularly forgot to send invoices for his salary. (FT <https://app.ft.com/content/9edd3730-3a15-4e1a-b33a-629aff00e847>)
The new investment banking structure is taking shape at BNP Paribas, with Mark Lynagh from the UK team and Sancho Ferran from Spain being named co-heads of EMEA investment banking. (Financial News <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/bnp-paribas-names-new-dealmaking-leaders-in-regional-shake-up-39d6228c>)
The most entertaining banking employment litigation in the Southern Hemisphere continues, and it seems that Dan Reynolds and Silvana Schenone will have to hand over data from their phones so that Jarden can quiz them about co-ordinated hiring for Barrenjoey. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/jarden-bankers-told-to-hand-over-phone-data-in-barrenjoey-fight?srnd=phx-india>)
Machine learning can spot patterns in people’s banking activity which are associated with the early signs of dementia – missed payments, large withdrawals or “an uncharacteristic fear of the stock market”. Perhaps the same software could be applied to trading desks to spot when bankers are losing their edge. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-11-13/how-financial-data-can-reveal-early-signs-of-dementia?srnd=homepage-uk>)

item.title: Hedge funds have got a hiring problem. It does not concern portfolio managers
item.description:
If you're a hedge fund looking to find a new portfolio manager, then good luck to you. The world may be awash with displaced investment talent </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>, but as Bobby Jain </news/bobby-jain-jain-global>noted last week it's not easy to find someone who can manage large amounts of money, construct a balanced portfolio </news/bobby-jain-jain-global> and stay cool during a drawdown.
Despite this, portfolio managers may not be the biggest hiring problem right now. The biggest hiring problem is people who can help them handle these difficult markets. Coaches.
“I think we have three coaches in EMEA and we’re trying to hire another one," says Reid Murphy, head of business development for Europe at Point72. "It’s harder to hire a coach than a PM, and I’ve run the hiring of both.”
Point72 has a long history of using coaches to assist its investment talent. Founder Steve Cohen used coaches in the prehistoric period of the early 1990s, and his lead coach of that era is seen as the inspiration for the coach in TV show Billions. Later in 2014, Cohen hired Gio Valiante, a college professor with a PhD in human motivation to help juice performance. Valiante left Point72 in 2020 but he still coaches funds on a consultancy basis and has worked with the likes of Citadel, Millennium and the deceased fund that was Eisler Capital.
Speaking earlier this year, Valiante said he runs "detachment exercises" for PMs (helping them to detach from regret over missed trades, to detach from fear that they won't make P&L in the future and to detach from concern for the opinions of other people). He encourages them to switch off over weekends. He helps them, “deploy capital proportional to the opportunity in the market in the moment.”
Like Murphy, Valiante says good coaches are like hens' teeth. Finding them is "terribly difficult," he tells us. "There's no barrier to entry so lots of complete frauds." Good ones are differentiated by a list of descriptors: "Training. Rigor. Different ways to help different investors. Honesty. Results."
Murphy didn't say how much these good coaches earn, but they are not cheap. This is partly because many have an investment background and must be persuaded to share their wisdom. Tom Ungi, </news/hedge-fund-coach> for example, was a head of trading and managing director at Millennium before he started coaching five years ago. Steven Goldstein was once a trader at Credit Suisse.
The coaches at Point72 are a "a huge investment," says Murphy. They're not making P&L themselves but they are former revenue generators and ex-PMs. "The bar for becoming a coach here is very high because that person has an impact on so many people. You have to be really, really good with people and really understand what each team is trying to accomplish.”
If this is you, you may want to get in touch.

item.title: "The only way to keep your junior financial services job now is to do this"
item.description:
This is a bad time to lose your job with a fund or a bank. The hiring market is slow. Whatever they might say, organisations do not really care about your future. This is why they are out there cutting the juniors they've only recently hired. </news/how-to-avoid-losing-junior-banking-job>
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
If you're a young person who has a job now, the number one thing you need to do is to find a MENTOR. I am speaking from 30 years' experience in this industry.
I am not talking about sycophancy. I am talking about finding someone who can genuinely guide you along a career path and who does care about you.
Finding this mentor is not easy. You must identify someone who is in a prominent position at the firm you work for and who you can learn from. If you choose correctly, it will transform your career.
The question is then how to make this mentor support you.
You must make yourself indispensable to them.
Rules 1,2,3,4 and 5 are "Don't f-up." Get the job done. Do extra stuff without them having to ask. Anticipate questions and have the answers to hand. DON'T make stuff up if you don't know it. Say you don't know, but find the answer asap.
All else is pointless. Even if you are a top performer </news/barclays-cut-hedge-fund-sales>you are not safe without this mentor on your side. Choose carefully and it will be transformative. If and when the mentor leaves, you will have a massive opportunity ahead if you have learned from them.
Boris Pugliese is the pseudonym of an anonymous hedge fund quant
